5615 <app><lem wit="#N">saviji sovaṅ</lem><rdg wit="#P"><gap reason="omitted"></gap></rdg></app>,
. <app><lem wit="#N">әnahakәna ri harәpiṅ saṅgar</lem><rdg wit="#P">harәpiṅ saṅgar</rdg></app>,
. <app><lem wit="#N">kaṅ riṅ saṅgar kadi kramaniṅ bantǝn kaṅ lagi-lagi,</lem><rdg wit="#P">harәpiṅ saṅgar, sampun marәp muṅgahakәna mariṅ saṅgar</rdg></app>
. kaṅ riṅ ibu,
. <app><lem wit="#N">kaṅ ri tәṅah</lem><rdg wit="#P">riṅ pagәneyan</rdg></app>,
5620 <app><lem wit="#N">vuhana burat vaṅi, lәṅa vaṅi, mvaṅ bәras, 2, catu, artha, 225, pinūjā saparikrama, taṅ abhakti, vusiṅ aṅabhakti,</lem><rdg wit="#P">kadi bantәn sisirih, malih muṅgah riṅ saṅgar, bәras, 2, catu, artha, 225, lә̥ṅa burat vaṅi, yen vus umūja paṅabhakti</rdg></app>
. <app><lem wit="#N">amaṅan sarimpǝn, ry uvusiṅ amaṅan sarimpǝn, amaṅan sakavaśa</lem><rdg wit="#P">yen vus aṅabhakti amaṅan haṅinuṅ· sakavasanya. </rdg></app>,
. <app><lem wit="#N">pūjāniṅ amaṅan sarimpǝn</lem><rdg wit="#P">nyan pūjānya</rdg></app>,
. om̐ paduka bhaṭārī sāriniṅ galuṅan, mānuṣanira kinavruhakǝn sāriniṅ galuṅan, aṅisǝp sāriniṅ rahina, aṅisǝp sāriniṅ vәṅi, aṅisǝp sāriniṅ śrī sādhana, aṅisǝp
. <app><lem wit="#N">sarvasāri</lem><rdg wit="#P">sāriniṅ sarvasāri</rdg></app>,
5625 aṅisǝp sāriniṅ
. <app><lem wit="#N">rāt bhuvana kabeh</lem><rdg wit="#P">sarvabhuvana, sakabeh riṅ hulun</rdg></app>,
. <app><lem wit="#N">hulun vruh sāriniṅ galuṅan</lem><rdg wit="#P"> vruh sariniṅ galuṅan</rdg></app>, andadi ya bhujaṅgga lәvih, akaḍaṅ
. <app><lem wit="#N">aratu</lem><rdg wit="#P">ratu</rdg></app>,
. sukha sugih śarīraniṅ hulun,
5630 <app><lem wit="#P">anak-anak akeḍәp</lem><rdg wit="#N">akanaka keḍәp,</rdg></app>
. aputu abuyut, tumus tumǝrus, təkaniṅ anak putu buyutiṅ hulun,
. <app><lem wit="#N">katəkana sapinakṣaniṅ hulun</lem><rdg wit="#P" cause="line_omission"></rdg></app>, saṅ hyaṅ triyodaśa sakṣi, anakṣeniṅ hulun, phalanya, siṅ kāryanta anәmu hayu,
. <app><lem wit="#N">kinasihan deniṅ</lem><rdg wit="#P">kinasihan</rdg></app> bhūta dәṅǝn, mvaṅ jәnǝk sahisiniṅ pomahan.
.<app>
5635<lem wit="#N #P"></lem>
.<note> nihan bratā hañarin ... sahisiniṅ pomahan
. <ptr target="#N"/>
. in 3.73 <ptr target="#P"/>
. in 3.113 </note>
5640</app>
.</ab>
.</div>
.

5645
.<!-- P hana bratā sussukan, ṅa, riṅ pūṛṇnamaniṅ kapitu, piṅ 7, sarahina piṅ, 7, savәṅi hamaṅan haṅinum, haṅigәl, bhaṭāra kapitu maveh bratā, phalanya suka sugih, hanakāmitra, diṛgha yuṣa, kedhәp kapintuhu -->
.
.<!-- U hana brātā susukān, ṅa, riṅ pūrṇnāmaniṅ kapitu, piṅ pitu sarahina, pi pitu savṅi, hamaṅana haṅinum haṅigәl, bhaṭāra kapitu maveh brātā, pa, suka sugih anak amitra, dirgghā yūṣā kedhәp kapintuhu -->
.

5690
.<!-- G hana brata, mavucandrā, sabran soma yan masipat, ůniveh buddha hir̥ṅ, dite manis, ůniveh sari-sari, saṅ hyaṅ manik badhe devatanya, satahun tigaṅ ṅlek samayanya, pha, masih saṅ hyaṅ candra ditya, tan lamūr katon ayu, pinicaya phalanya -->
.

.

.

.
.

5895 yaniṅ vәṅi sәḍǝṅ sirәpiṅ voṅ, limaṅ lek lavasanya,

.
5910<!-- N hana brata, hañjaya, ṅa, tan pamaṅan yan liṅsiṛ, satahun pituṅ dinā lavasanya, saṅ hyaṅ kr̥tta bhuvana hyaṅniṅ brata, pha, kr̥tta kaṅ rāt, manuh kaṅ pr̥mana, sidḍi kanisihan deniṅ hyaṅ, kineriṅan deniṅ saṛvva galak-->
.
.<!-- P hana bratā hañjaya, kramanya tan pamaṅan yan lisiṛ savaṛṣa pituṅ dinā samayanya saṅ hyaṅ kr̥tta bhuvana hyaṅ niṅ bratā, kr̥tta taṅ rāt, manuh kaṅ pr̥maṇa, phalanya siddi kinasihan deniṅ hyaṅ, kineriṅan deniṅ saṛvva galak -->
.
.
5915
.

.

.
.

5955<div type="subchapter" n="3.88">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_88">hana brata
. <app><lem wit="#P">anrus</lem><rdg wit="#N">nrus</rdg></app>
. tuñjuṅ,

5960 <app><lem wit="#N">yaniṅ</lem><rdg wit="#P">yan riṅ</rdg></app>

5965 yan paṅloṅ, piṅ, 14, haśeva latrī, acaru śuci sadaṇdhanan, bhaṭāra guru

. <abbr>pha</abbr>,

.<lem wit="#N #P"></lem>

.<!-- N hana bratā, haturū haṅadǝg, sabhāgya yen aṅeka padḍa pisan, pituṅ vṅi samayanyā, yen kita hamaṅan sakpǝl sarahina, yan aṅinūm bañu sahlǝd, tluṅ dinā, tluṅ vṅi samayanya, pha, sapocapan riṅ devā, byakta śakti tkeṅ kamokṣan -->
6665
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.119">

.<ptr target="#N"/>
. in 3.119 </note>
6675</app>

.
.
6680
.<!-- N hana bratā, maṅan rvaṅ kpǝl , pituṅ vṅi lavasānya, guṇa mogha ḍataṅ, tan kevu han , phalanya, Anidra ṅaraniṅ bratā maṅkana -->
.

6730
.<!-- N hana bratā, maṅan pituṅ kpǝl, saptā latri lavasanya, guṇa mogha ḍataṅ, saṛvva viṣā tan kataman kittha, yeka phalanya, catūṛ mukā ṅaraniṅ brata maṅkana -->
.
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.123">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_123">hana brata, maṅan pituṅ kәpǝl, sapta latri lavasanya, guṇa moga ḍatәṅ,
6735 <app><lem type="norm">sarvaviṣya</lem><rdg wit="#N">sarvaviṣa</rdg></app>

. <app><lem wit="#N">siddha sakāryanta</lem><rdg wit="#P">siddha sakahyunta</rdg></app>,
. <app><lem wit="#N">tan pamaṅgih kevǝh</lem><rdg wit="#P">siddha kapaṅgih</rdg></app>.
7495 <app><lem wit="#N #P"></lem>
. <note> hana brata, kumavaśa ... pamaṅgih kevǝh <note>
. </note>
. <ptr target="#N"/> in III.161 <ptr target="#P"/> in III.83 </note>
.</app>
7500</ab>
.</div>
.
.
.
7505
.
.
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.162">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_162">hana brata, niṅibu,
7510 <abbr>ṅa</abbr>, amaṅan sarvaibu, pataṅ lek divaśanya,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>, mulih riṅ
. <supplied reason="omitted">svarga</supplied>
. bhaṭāra rudra, sasarnya majanma riṅ kula, <sic>saṅ kumbhakarṇa, aturu tan paṅlihan, rahina vәṅi tur aṅupavāśa, pha, keḍәp saparipolahta.</sic>
.</ab>
7515</div>
.
.
.
.<!-- N hana brata, tan pamaṅan tan paturū, saṅ hyaṅ tan kaviśeṣā hyaṅnya, pha, svaṛggā titisnya -->
7520<!-- P hana bratā, tan paṅan tan paturu, brata saṅ hyaṅ tan kaviśeṣan, ṅa, phalnya svaṛgga titisnya -->
.
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.163">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_163">hana brata, tan
. <app><lem wit="#N">pamaṅan</lem><rdg wit="#P">paṅan</rdg></app>
7525 tan paturu,
. <app><lem wit="#N">saṅ</lem><rdg wit="#P">brata saṅ</rdg></app>
. hyaṅ tan
. <app><lem wit="#N">kaviśeṣa,</lem><rdg wit="#P">kaviśeṣan</rdg></app>
. <app><lem wit="#N">hyaṅnya</lem><rdg wit="#P"><gap reason="omitted"></gap></rdg></app>,
7530 <app><lem wit="#N"><abbr>pha</abbr></lem><rdg wit="#P">ṅa, phalnya</rdg></app>,
. svarga titisnya.
.<app><lem wit="#N #P"></lem>
. <note> hana brata, tan ... svaṛggā titisnya <note>
. </note>
7535 <ptr target="#N"/> in III.164 <ptr target="#P"/> in III.113 </note>
.</app>
.</ab>
.</div>
.
7540
.
.
.<!-- N hana bratā, l̥vih turu, ṅa, tan tr̥ṣṇeṅ paṅān, bhaṭāri keśavā hyaṅiṅ brata, pha, mantuk riṅ svaṛgga bhaṭāra śivā, mañjanmā ri kula putra, luputiṅ lara vighnā, subhāga hanulus -->
.<!-- P hana brata l̥vih turu, ṅa, tan tr̥ṣṇeṅ paṅan, bhaṭāra keśava hyaṅnya, phalanya mantuk riṅ svaṛggan bhaṭāra śiva, mañjanma riṅ kula putra, luputiṅ saṛvva vighna, subhaga anulus -->
7545
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.164">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_164">hana brata, lәvih turu,
. <abbr>ṅa</abbr>,
. tan trәṣṇeṅ paṅān, bhaṭārī keśava
7550 <app><lem wit="#N">hyaṅiṅ brata</lem><rdg wit="#P">hyaṅnya</rdg></app>,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>,
. mantuk riṅ
. <app><lem wit="#N">svarga</lem><rdg wit="#P">svargan</rdg></app>
. bhaṭāra śiva, mañjanma ri kulaputra, luputiṅ lara vighna, subhaga anulus.
7555<app><lem wit="#N #P"></lem>
. <note> hana bratā, l̥vih ... subhāga hanulus <note>
. </note>
. <ptr target="#N"/> in III.165 <ptr target="#P"/> in III.116 </note>
.</app>
7560
.</ab>
.</div>
.
.
7565
.
.
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.165">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_165">hana brata, mopavāsa pituṅ
7570 rātri, atәhәr tan kәneṅ turu rahina vәṅi, bhaṭāra śīva hyaṅiṅ brata,
. <abbr>ma</abbr>,
. om̐ nāma śivāya, pamit,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>,
. <app><lem type="emn">vīryavan</lem><rdg wit="#N">viyavan</rdg></app> ,
7575 <supplied reason="omitted">pha</supplied>,
. sakāryanta siddha, tәhәr siddhi.
.</ab>
.</div>
.
7580
.<!-- N hana brata ambhira, ṅa, yan hamaṅan mevakā Uyah kevalā, satahun tigaṅ lek ṣamayanya, pha, prih meṅgal katmu, deva bhūtha sih iri kittha -->
.
.<!-- P hana brata mbira, ṅa, yan hamaṅan mevak huyah kevala, satavun lavasnyā mvaṅ tigaṅ lek ṣamayanya, bhaṭāra Iśvara hyaṅnya. ma, Ōm̐ mam̐ Iśvara ya namaḥ. phalanya siṅ prih Eṅgāl katәmu tuṛ kinasihan deniṅ devabhuṭa, kinasihan deniṅ rāt -->
.
7585<!-- U hana bratāmbira, ṅa, yan amaṅan mevaka huyah, satahun tigaṅṅ lek samayanya, bhaṭāreśvara hyaṅnya, ma, om̐ mam̐ Iśvara ya namaḥ, pamit, pha, siṅ pinrih heṅgal katmu, kinasihiṅ rāt kita, mvaṅ deva bhutāsihi ri kita -->
.
.
.
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.166">
7590<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_166">hana brata
. <app><lem type="norm">ambīra</lem><rdg wit="#N #U">ambhira</rdg><rdg wit="#P">mbira</rdg></app>,
. <abbr>ṅa</abbr>,
. yan amaṅan
. <app><lem wit="#N #U">mevaka</lem><rdg wit="#P">mevaka</rdg></app>
7595 uyah kevala, satahun
. <app><lem wit="#N #U">tigaṅ lek samayanya</lem><rdg wit="#P">lavasnya mvaṅ tigaṅ lek samayanya</rdg></app>,
. <app><lem wit="#P">bhaṭāra iśvara hyaṅnya,</lem><rdg wit="#U">bhaṭāreśvara hyaṅnya</rdg><rdg wit="#N"><gap reason="omitted"></gap></rdg></app>
. <app><lem wit="#P #U"><abbr>ma</abbr>, om̐ mam̐ Iśvarāya namaḥ</lem><rdg wit="#N"><gap reason="omitted"></gap></rdg></app>
. <abbr>pha</abbr>,
7600 <app><lem wit="#P">siṅ prih</lem><rdg wit="#N">prih</rdg><rdg wit="#U">siṅ pinrih</rdg></app>
. <app><lem wit="#N">meṅgal</lem><rdg wit="#P #U">eṅgal</rdg></app>
. katәmu,
. <app><lem wit="#U">kinasihiṅ rāt kita,</lem><rdg wit="#N"><gap reason="omitted"></gap></rdg><rdg wit="#P" cause="transposition">tur kinasihan deniṅ rāt</rdg></app>
. <app><lem wit="#U">mvaṅ deva bhūta sih iri kita</lem><rdg wit="#N">deva bhūta sih iri kita</rdg><rdg wit="#P" cause="transposition">tur kinasihan deniṅ deva bhūta</rdg></app>.
7605
.<app><lem wit="#N #P #U"></lem>
.<note> hana brata ambhira... kita<note>
.</note>
.<ptr target="#N"/> in III.167 <ptr target="#P"/> in III.30 <ptr target="#U"/> in III.13 </note>
7610</app>
.</ab>
.</div>
.
.
7615
.
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.167">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_167">hana brata aṅlavar, ṅa, tan pamaṅaniṅ uyahan, satahun divasanya, bhaṭāra śaṅkara hyaṅnya,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>, mulih riṅ kendran, sasarnya majanma riṅ
7620 <app><lem type="norm">lituhayu</lem><rdg wit="#N">listvayu</rdg></app>
. prajña kita. </ab>
.</div>
.
.
7625
.
.<!-- N hana brata, ṅlavar, ṅa, tan pamaṅan huyah, pat vulan ptaṅ vṅi samayanya, bhaṭāra saṅkara hyaṅnya,pha, mantuk mariṅ kendran, sasaṛnya mañjanmā listuhayu paripuṛṇnā -->
.<!-- P hana bratā ṅlavaṛ, ṅa, tan pamaṅan huyah, pat ulan pәtaṅ vәṅi samayanya, bhaṭāra saṅkāra hyaṅnya, phalanyā, sasaṛnya mañjanmā listuhayu paripūrṇna -->
.
7630<div type="subchapter" n="3.168">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_168">hana brata, ṅlavar,
. <abbr>ṅa</abbr>, tan pamaṅan uyah, pat vulan pәtaṅ vәṅi samayanya, bhaṭāra śaṅkara hyaṅnya,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>,
. <app><lem wit="#N">mantuk mariṅ kendran</lem><rdg wit="#P"><gap reason="omitted"></gap></rdg></app>, sasarnya
7635 mañjanma lituhayu paripūrṇa.
. <app><lem wit="#N #P"></lem>
. <note> hana brata, ṅlavar ... listuhayu paripuṛṇnā <note>
. </note>
. <ptr target="#N"/> in III.169 <ptr target="#P"/> in III.81 </note>
7640</app>
.</ab>
.</div>
.
.
7645
.
.
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.169">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_169">hana brata, aṅupavāsa,
7650 <abbr>ṅa</abbr>,
. lamun amaṅan aṅgugut uyah arәṅ rumuhun, 3, tahun divasanya, bhaṭārī gaṅga hyaṅniṅ brata,
. <abbr>ma</abbr>, om̐
. <app><lem type="emn">gaṅgāyai</lem><rdg wit="#N">gaṅgāya</rdg></app>
. nama svāhā,
7655 <abbr>pha</abbr>,
. saparipolahta kinerәṅan deniṅ jagat.
.</ab>
.</div>
.
7660
.
.
.<!-- N hana brata, maṅan tumpǝṅ hivak huyah har̥ṅ, bhaṭāra Iśvara hyaṅnya, ya pinakarūpā, pinakāśvaraniṅ kiduṅ caritta, pha, manisiṅ panutukan -->
.<!-- P hana brata maṅan tumpәṅ hivaknya huyah har̥ṅ, pәtaṅ tavun samayanya, kinasihan deniṅ padhanta janmā -->
7665
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.170">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_170">hana brata, maṅan tumpǝṅ
. <app><lem type="emn">mevak</lem><rdg wit="#N">ivak</rdg></app> uyah harәṅ, bhaṭāra iśvara hyaṅnya, ya pinakarūpa, pinakaśvaraniṅ kiduṅ carita,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>, manisiṅ panutukan.
7670 <app><lem wit="#N #P"></lem>
. <note> hana brata, maṅan ... manisiṅ panutukan <note>
. </note>
. <ptr target="#N"/> in III.171 <ptr target="#P"/> quite similiar, but different in the technique and the result. Here is the P: hana brata maṅan tumpәṅ ivaknya huyah harәṅ, pәtaṅ tavun samayanya, kinasihan deniṅ padhanta janma </note>
.</app>
7675</ab>
.</div>
.
.
.
7680
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.171">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_171">hana brata, amaṅan kǝmbaṅ, naṅkǝn,
. <abbr>U</abbr>,
. <app><lem type="emn">mevak</lem><rdg wit="#N">ivak</rdg></app>
7685 uyah harәṅ, vusiṅ amaṅan, aṅinaṅ suruh pupucuk, aṅliṅga kǝmbaṅ,
. <abbr>ṅa</abbr>,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>,
. sukha sugih, rūpa aheṅ.
.</ab>
7690</div>
.
.
.
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.172">
7695<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_172">hana brata, amaṅan tan pauyah, pituṅ vәṅi samayanya,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>,
. śaktinta ḍatәṅ, tәhәr kinatvaṅan deniṅ hyaṅ. </ab>
.</div>
.
7700
.
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.173">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_173">hana brata, amaṅan
. arasotih,
7705 <abbr>ṅa</abbr>, aḍahar uyah harәṅ
. <app><lem type="norm">pinakavulam</lem><rdg wit="#N">minakavulam</rdg></app>,
. lama pituṅ dina, ra nini paduka bhaṭārī
. <app><lem type="emn">sarasvatī</lem><rdg wit="#N">śarasoti</rdg></app>
. hyaṅniṅ brata,
7710 <abbr>pha</abbr>, prajñan.
.</ab>
.</div>
.
.
7715<div type="subchapter" n="3.174">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_174">nihan kr̥ta māsa,
. <abbr>ṅa</abbr>,
. hayuniṅ hulun,
. <app><lem type="emn">akārya</lem><rdg wit="#N">sakārya</rdg></app>
7720 hayu, makadi vatǝk abrata, nūt avarah,</ab>
.
.<p n="1">śaśih ka, 1, taṅ, piṅ, 10, saṅ hyaṅ vīra kusuma devatanya, bratanya, hayva maṅan sarvabuṅkah,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>, sugih anom
. <app><lem type="conj">drәman</lem><rdg wit="#N"></rdg></app> avǝvәka ta sira.</p>
7725
.<p n="2">śaśih, 2, taṅ, piṅ, 7, saṅ hyaṅ jaya kusuma devatanya, bratanya hayva maṅan sapi,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>, luputeṅ tuju tәluh tarañjana, drәman ahiven iven.</p>
.
.<p n="3"> śaśih, 3, taṅ, piṅ, 9, saṅ hyaṅ naka devatanya, bratanya, hayva maṅan bavi,
7730 <abbr>pha</abbr>, tan katampǝkan gәriṅ aguṅ.</p>
.
.<p n="4">śaśih, 4, taṅ, piṅ, 15, saṅ hyaṅ asmara devatanya, bratanya, hayva maṅan sarvaroṇḍon,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>,
. dadi siṅ tinandur.</p>
7735
.<p n="5">śaśih, 5, paṅloṅ, piṅ, 15, saṅ hyaṅ mahādeva devatanya, bratanya, hayva sǝhǝk yan aṅūcap, hayva <app><lem type="emn">ṅǝmban</lem><rdg wit="#N">nǝṅbaṅ</rdg></app>
. boñcah,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>, drәman avǝvәka.</p>
.
7740<p n="6">śaśih, 6, taṅ, piṅ, 8, saṅ hyaṅ atanu devatanya, bratanya, hayva aṅinǝp, riṅ paluluṅhān,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>,
. sugih tan kelaṅ elaṅan.</p>
.
.<p n="7">śaśih, 7, taṅ, piṅ, 13, saṅ hyaṅ manasija devatanya, bratanya, aṅrakā,
7745 <abbr>pha</abbr>,
. sugih keḍәp kapaṅgih siṅ giṇa harṣa.</p>
.
.<p n="8">śaśih, 8, taṅ, piṅ, 2, saṅ hyaṅ anaṅgara devatanya, bratanya, hayva amaṅan paṭik vǝnaṅ suku pat,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>, sugih patik vǝnaṅ.</p>
7750
.<p n="9">śaśih, 9, taṅ, piṅ, 6, saṅ hyaṅ ravi devatanya, bratanya, hayva maṅan asu,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>,
. apәkik raspati prajurit.</p>
.
7755<p n="10">śaśih, 10, taṅ, piṅ, 4, saṅ hyaṅ brahmā devatanya, bratanya, hayva maṅan andǝlәṅ riṅ luhur, <abbr>pha</abbr>, kinasihaniṅ hyaṅ, mvaṅ voṅ mule
. <app><lem type="norm">akveh</lem><rdg wit="#N">akeh</rdg></app>
. asih iri kita.</p>
.
.<p n="11">śaśih, jyeṣṭa, taṅ, piṅ, 5, saṅ hyaṅ leka jaya devatanya, bratanya, aṅlampar ananapu,
7760 <abbr>pha</abbr>, keḍәp mandi sakәcapta.</p>
.
.<p n="12">śaśih, saddhā, taṅ, piṅ, 1, saṅ hyaṅ pisodharī devatanya, bratanya, hayva turu lavan istri, <abbr>pha</abbr>,
. keḍәp aomah omah.</p>
.
7765<p>Iyā ṅitaṅ kariṅ vulan, kr̥ta masa haranya, den asthiti sira, keṅәtakәna
. <app><lem type="norm">hayva</lem><rdg wit="#N">yva</rdg></app> lupa.</p>
.</div>
.
.
7770
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.175">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_175">hana brata, saninigraha,
. <abbr>ṅa</abbr>,
. tan mamati aghni ri kālaniṅ tumpǝk kalivon<supplied reason="omitted">,</supplied>
7775 <app><lem type="emn">molaha</lem><rdg wit="#N">moliha</rdg></app>
. sapuluh tumpәk kalivon,
. kramanya
. <app><lem type="emn">amuja</lem><rdg wit="#P">tamumuja</rdg></app>,
. ananapuh eṅ saṅgar,
7780 <app><lem type="emn">amvit</lem><rdg wit="#N">tāmvit</rdg></app>
. anǝmbaha ri bhaṭāra śīvāditya, lviriṅ caru riṅ saṅgar, anapunar, arih, rәmbaṅ, tambo lagu akah araka, phala, kambaṅ vaṅi, burat vaṅi, lәṅa vaṅi, sәḍǝṅan ikṣu, dīpa, dhūpa, den asaṅkǝp, devadarv inasab, vīja, dhūpa, ika kahatur i bhaṭāra,
. <abbr>ma</abbr>,
. om̐ namo bhagavatye vaśūdevāya, sarvatuṣṭan, dadāsime, om̐ śrī gurubhyo namaḥ, devacarundādasi mahātrәpti svāhā.</ab>
. <ab>tәlas ta ṅavaṅia ta kita,
7785 <abbr>ma</abbr>,
. om̐ sūrya putrāya namaḥ.
. samaṅkana taṅ brata lәkasakәna, hayva ta pramada riṅ brata, kunaṅ yan kālaṅan agriṅ, sakalviraniṅ aṅalaṅana, pinakavuruṅaniṅ brata, hayva pinakṣakǝn ikaṅ brata, kaliṅanya mvitana juga muvah, kunaṅ yan tan kalaṅana, anulus rahayu, pakṣakәna ika,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>,
. riṅ dlāhanta dadi ratu sukha vāhya katәmu, pinakāśraya deniṅ paḍanta ratu, keḍәp kapintuhu deniṅ rāt kabeh.</ab>
7790</div>
.
.
.
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.177">
7795<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_177">iti
. <app><lem type="conj">sāriniṅ</lem><rdg wit="#N" cause="haplography">sani</rdg></app>
. brata, kayatnakәna de saṅ
. <app><lem type="emn">amet</lem><rdg wit="#N"></rdg></app>
. hayu, ndan ika hayva malәtuh ikaṅ ambǝk, mataṅyan ika hayva
7800 <app><lem type="emn">mithya</lem><rdg wit="#N">miṣya</rdg></app> buddhi, tātkalanta maṅanakǝn brata, apan yan tan karakṣa ikaṅ brata denta, maṅdadyakǝn vighnaniṅ śarīra, yan enak denta rumakṣa sarīra, makajñāna buddhi mahottama, malilaṅa ahniṅ nirāvaraṇa, tan
. <app><lem type="emn">pagәlәh-gәlәh</lem><rdg wit="#N"></rdg></app>,
. tan karakәtan karṇa śūla, mvaṅ rajah tamah, ika ta maṅdadyakǝn svarga magәṅ, ṅuniveh jñāna viśeṣa, vruha ri kramanira sovaṅ-sovaṅ.
.</ab>
.</div>
7805
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.178">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_178">hana brata sabran
. <app><lem type="emn">umanis</lem><rdg wit="#N">manis</rdg></app>,
. <abbr>ṅa</abbr>,
7810 tan pamaṅan tampakiṅ apuy, rvaṅ vulan samayanya,
.sabran pahiṅ tan pamaṅan tampakiṅ aghni, rvaṅ vulan samayanya,
.sabran pon tan padus tan palәṅa, tan pararavup, tan pakәkәmuh, rvaṅ vulan samayanya,
.sabran vage, tan paturu gumuliṅ, rvaṅ vulan samayanya,
.sabran kalivon, tan paṅucap-ucap, rvaṅ vulan samayanya,
7815<abbr>pha</abbr>,
. ginañjar deniṅ vatǝk devata kabeh, norana nūkr̥tani, tan hilaṅ takonakәna, drәventa tǝmbe.
.
.</ab>
.</div>
7820
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.179">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_179">nihan haji pabrata, yaniṅ taṅgal piṅ lima, anuju kalivon, paṅupavāśa,</ab>
.<p n="1"> esuknya riṅ
. <app><lem type="norm">umanis</lem><rdg wit="#N">manis</rdg></app>, amaṅan kupat pāṇḍava, 5, ivaknya kacaṅ,
7825 <abbr>pha</abbr>,
. dukiṅ alit duruṅ anәmu, yan vus agәṅ amaṅgih sukha sugih aguṅ dunya.</p>
.
.<p n="2"><abbr>pa</abbr>,
. amaṅan kupat syaṅ anti, 9, ivaknya komak,
7830 <abbr>pha</abbr>, tinuṅgu deniṅ rāma reṇa, aṅantos aputu abuyut, kinadhama deniṅ bapebu,
. <app><lem type="emn">kapti deniṅ</lem><rdg wit="#N">kaptini</rdg></app> hulun.</p>
.
.<p n="3"><abbr>pva</abbr>,
. amaṅan kupat sidayu, 7, ivaknya sudhaṅ,
7835 <abbr>pha</abbr>, aṅapti listvayu, alit arampiṅ aṅlәlǝnte, tan amadhani, sukha sugih drәman baṅkit, pinarәkan pinakapahulunaniṅ maru. </p>
.
.<p n="4"> <abbr>va</abbr>,
. amaṅan kupat sih tan pәgat, 4, ivaknya taluh,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>, aṅapti sukha sugih, drәman siddhi baṅkit, keḍәpiṅ alaki, tan kavaśa lakinta aṅluṅani, pinūji deniṅ matva, tanana ṅesǝm.</p>
7840
.<p n="5"> <abbr>ka</abbr>,
. <supplied reason="omitted">amaṅan</supplied>
. aṇḍa kupat gәnǝp, 8, ivaknya raraśmen,
. <abbr>pha,</abbr>
7845 aṅapti sukha sugih aguṅ vīrya, añjǝnǝṅ arddha nareśvarī, keḍәp aṅucap.
. </p>
.<p n="6"> esuk riṅ
. <app><lem type="norm">umanis</lem><rdg wit="#N">manis</rdg></app>,
. <supplied reason="omitted">amaṅan</supplied>
7850 aṇḍa kupat siddha luṅguh, 10, ivaknya dagiṅ loh, sāgara dhanu, alas savah, dagiṅ pomahan,
. <supplied reason="omitted">pha,</supplied>
. aṅapti sukha sugih aguṅ vīrya, kinajrihan deniṅ śatru, kinadama deniṅ bala mvaṅ varga, pinarәkan deniṅ bala
. <app><lem type="norm">sabraṅ</lem><rdg wit="#N">sabran</rdg></app>,
. tan
7855 <app><lem type="emn">kevaṅan</lem><rdg wit="#N">ivaṅ</rdg></app>
. deniṅ bala, sami vatra tan anaṅsal, siddhi maṇḍi tan paṅucap, rәmrәm ikaṅ vvaṅ kabeh, riṅ panaṅkilan, tinaṅkiliṅ bala sakiṅ doh, abahan təka sakiṅ tan hana, sabran-sabran, yan vadon sinivi deniṅ maru, tan hana maḍani, sadera ṅrehakәna, vr̥ddhi putra, kinajrihan deniṅ santana, vīrya bhukti, embuh mañabuh, imbuh-imbuh tan paṅloṅ. sami danur daha.
.</p>
.</div>
.
7860
.<!-- G hana brāta nuṅkurat, ṅa, kalivon hama, manis amadhuhara, pahiṅ habāyu hara, pvan atoya hara, vage haghnihara, pūṛṇnama tiḷm hamatihara, piṅ rvana kabeh Ika, hakabeh phalanya, hamupiṅ brata kabeh -->

.

.<!-- N hana bratā, mañcadara, ṅa, manis hamaṅan sga putih, pahiṅ hamāṅan ktan bāṅ, pvan hamaṅān sga kuniṅ, vage hamaṅan ktan īr̥ṅ, kalivon hamaṅan ktan hamañca vārṇna||0|| vetan hamaṅan hantǝlu putihnya, kidul surā, kulon hantǝlu kuniṅ, loṛ bakakul, riṅ tṅah śarasi bāṅ hāti, pha, suka sugih-->
.
.<!-- U hana bratā mañca vara, ṅa, manis humaṅan sgā putih, pahiṅ hamaṅan laktan bāṅ, pon hamaṅan sgā kuniṅ, vage hamaṅan ktan hir̥ṅ, kalivon, hamaṅan ktan amañca varṇna, ṅa, vetan hamaṅan sgā putih mvah Āntәlu putihnya, kidul sura, kulon hantalu kuniṅnya, lor bakatul, riṅ tṅah sarasi bāṅ hatih, pha, suka sugih -->
7895
.
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.181">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_181">hana brata,
. <app><lem wit="#U">mañcavāra</lem><rdg wit="#N">mañcavara</rdg></app>,
7900 <abbr>ṅa</abbr>,

. <app><lem wit="#N">amaṅan</lem><rdg wit="#U">umaṅan</rdg></app>
. sәga putih, pahiṅ amaṅan
. <app><lem wit="#N">kәtan</lem><rdg wit="#U">lakәtan</rdg></app>
7905 baṅ,
. <app><lem wit="#U">pon</lem><rdg wit="#N">pvan</rdg></app>
. amaṅan sәga kuniṅ, vage amaṅan kәtan irәṅ, kalivon amaṅan kәtan amañca varṇa.
. vetan amaṅan
. <app><lem wit="#N">antǝlu putihnya</lem><rdg wit="#U">sәga putih mvah antәlu putihnya</rdg></app>, kidul sura, kulon antǝlu
7910 <app><lem wit="#N">kuniṅ</lem><rdg wit="#U">kuniṅnya</rdg></app>,
. lor
. <app><lem wit="#N">bakakul</lem><rdg wit="#U">bakatul</rdg></app>,
. riṅ tәṅah śarasi baṅ
. <app><lem wit="#N">hati</lem><rdg wit="#U">atih</rdg></app>,
7915 <abbr>pha</abbr>,
. sukha sugih.
. <app><lem wit="#N #U"></lem>
. <note> hana bratā, mañcadara ... sukha sugih <note>
. </note>
7920 <ptr target="#N"/> in III.180 <ptr target="#U"/> in III.80 </note>
.</app>

.
7925
.
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.182">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_182">hana brata, anūt saptavāra,

7930 <abbr>ra</abbr>, asisirih, 5,
. <abbr>ra</abbr>.

7935 <abbr>a</abbr>.

.<div type="subchapter" n="3.183">

. <abbr>pha</abbr>,
. tәḍunaniṅ drәman agave hayu, tan kapәjahan vәka kita, tәrus tumus tәkeṅ vәka vet bet.
7955</ab>

.
.
.
7960<div type="subchapter" n="3.184">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_184">hana brata, maṅan sәkul saravup, sinaṅga ri taṅan kiva, tan patәḍa tan patambǝh,
. <supplied reason="omitted">ivaknya</supplied>

7965 saṅ hyaṅ sandi rasa sira turun abrata, uṅgvanira riṅ śarīra, riṅ rahasya,

.</ab>
.</div>
7970
.
.
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.185">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_185">hana brata, amaṅan sinaṅga ri taṅan kiva, saivaknya, sagәlǝmiṅ abrata, pakṣa hiḍǝp,
7975 <abbr>ṅa</abbr>,

. <supplied reason="omitted"><abbr>pha</abbr></supplied>,

7980</div>
.

7985 <abbr>pha</abbr>, akveh mahyun iri kita, anva ṅaraniṅ brata maṅkana.

.
.
7990<div type="subchapter" n="3.187">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_187">hana brata, maṅan sәga kevala, sagәlǝmiṅ abrata, hyaṅ puravat sira turun abrata,

7995</div>

.

.

. baṅ, 5,

. brata, 5, mañcavāra, saṅ hyaṅ padma rasa tumurun
. <app><lem wit="#N">abrata</lem><rdg wit="#U">brata</rdg></app>,

8050 <app><lem wit="#N">śabda</lem><rdg wit="#U"><gap reason="omitted"></gap></rdg></app>

8065
.<!-- N hana bratā, hañkul haṅgi, hulam pahi, laṅa tṅah lek, ranini paduka bhaṭārī Uma hyaṅ niṅ brata, pha, vavanon vastu, kinarmmakniṅ hakeh -->
.

.

. aṅgi, ulam pahi,

8075 <app><lem wit="#N">satәṅah</lem><rdg wit="#U">tәṅah</rdg></app>
. lek, ranini paduka bhaṭārī uma hyaṅniṅ brata,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>,
. <app><lem type="norm">avavanon</lem><rdg wit="#N">wawanon</rdg><rdg wit="#U">vavadon</rdg></app> <app><lem wit="#N">vastu</lem><rdg wit="#U">svasta</rdg></app>,
. kinarmakәniṅ
8080 <app><lem type="norm">akveh</lem><rdg wit="#N #U">akeh</rdg></app>.</ab>
.<app><lem wit="#N #U"></lem>
. <note> hana bratā, hañkul ... kinarmmakniṅ hakeh <note>
. </note>
. <ptr target="#N"/> in III.190 <ptr target="#U"/> in III.102 </note>
8085</app>
.</div>
.
.
.
8090<div type="subchapter" n="3.192">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_192">hana brata, amaṅan sәkul aṅgi, anaṅgap, 7,

. sira saṅ hyaṅ viśeṣa tumurun abrata,

8095 ginañjaran śakti lima, vadon viṣṇu anәmu, tan

8100
.
.
.
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.193">
8105<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_193">hana brata, amaṅan sәkul pañcavarṇa, aren tiniṅkah cakra
.tinañcǝban vr̥ti, denta maṅan maṅkana tatkāla kalivon, añakra bhuvana,
.<abbr>ṅa</abbr>, saṅ hyaṅ śivātma sira turun abrata, ya pinakarūpa, pinakayuṣa, pinakalaku,
. <supplied reason="omitted"><abbr>pha,</abbr> </supplied>
. dadi vvaṅ aṅuripi jagat, sukha sugih vәnaṅ pinakasāriniṅ jagat, riṅ niṣkala.
8110</ab>
.</div>
.
.
.
8115
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.194">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_194">hana brata jaga varṇa,
. <abbr>ṅa</abbr>, amaṅan sәkul, balañan <supplied reason="omitted">,</supplied>
. pituṅ vәṅi samayanya,
8120 <abbr>pha</abbr>,
. keḍәp deniṅ rāt, prajñan vicakṣaṇa, bisāgamǝl aṅiduṅ, vīryavan.
.</ab>

.
8125
.
.
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.195">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_195">hana brata, yan amaṅan anǝmbah sәkul, pituṅ rātri divasanya,
8130 <abbr>pha</abbr>,
. kinasihaniṅ hyaṅ, śrī cittāmaṇi ṅaraniṅ brata maṅkana.
.</ab>
.</div>
.
8135
.
.
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.196">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_196">hana brata naṅga sәkul, tinumpaṅan vr̥tti, yan pәjah ikaṅ vr̥ti, pavusan kita pamaṅan, pituṅ vәṅi lavasanya, <supplied reason="omitted"><abbr>pha,</abbr></supplied> salviriṅ
8140 <app><lem type="conj">sañjata</lem><rdg wit="#N"></rdg></app>
. tan tame kita, aṅañcaṅ ṅaraniṅ brata maṅkana.

.
8145
.
.
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.197">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_197">hana brata, yan amaṅan tinañcǝban vr̥tti
8150 vulan, saṅ hyaṅ anuṅkǝbi jagat hyaṅnya, ya minakarūpā hayu apәkik,
. <supplied reason="omitted">pha</supplied>
. riṅ dadi vvaṅ sukha sugih, vәnaṅ amatūt jagat riṅ niṣkala.</ab>

.
8155
.
.
.
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.198">
8160<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_198">hana brata, amaṅan tinañcǝban tuṅgul, tiniṅkah bhīma, hyaṅ maṇik teja,
. <abbr>ṅa</abbr>,
. saṅ hyaṅ paṅirut jagat turuna abrata, ya pinakarūpa, pinakalaku, pinakateja,
. <supplied reason="omitted">pha,</supplied> aśrī iṅiriṅ sañjata, sakṣat kǝmbaṅ tinuṅgulan, śakti aṅrәbahakǝn jagat riṅ niṣkala.
.</ab>
8165</div>
.
.
.
.
8170
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.199">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_199">hana brata, avr̥ti,
. <abbr>ṅa</abbr>,
. yan amaṅan tinañcǝban vr̥tti, pәjah taṅ vr̥tti, avusan amaṅan, saptarātri divasanya,
8175 <abbr>pha</abbr>, sarvaroga tan tumameṅ śarīranta.
.</ab>
.</div>
.
.
8180
.
.
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.200">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_200">hana brata, aṅǝmbaṅ,
8185 <abbr>ṅa</abbr>,

. <abbr>pha</abbr>,
. deva sih iri kita.</ab>
.</div>
8190
.
.
.

.<div type="subchapter" n="3.292">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_291">[nyan ta saṅ citta varaṇā, umarah
. <supplied reason="omitted">ri</supplied>
.<ab>saṅ vala kula, mūla tattvaniṅ dadi kabeh, pahenak paṅrәṅə̄nta, mūlabhoktaniṅ kanirāśrayan, mvaṅ kābhyudayan, bhāvanya mvaṅ lakṣaṇanya, pūrvanya mvaṅ vәkasnya, maṅkana liṅ saṅ vala kula, nǝmbah hulun, om̐ viku satakvan tānaku, kita pva śikṣā ṅaran ika, duga-duga tumakvan, vuvus maṅkana, rәṅə̄n siptaniṅ hulun.</ab>
9760<ab>
.<foreign>pūrvaṃ śrī puruṣānte, varānugraha makanya, saṅ rojyam, narāsakane, ayavaṃ vidyāṃ prajayaṃ.</foreign>
.</ab>
.
.<ab>
9765maṅkana pariñciniṅ cipta, kaliṅanya, pūrva haraniṅ mimitan, tripuruṣa haraniṅ brahmā viṣṇu īśvara, vara ṅaraniṅ amidhi, anugraha haraniṅ panuṅsuṅ, manoka ṅaraniṅ devata, saroja ṅaraniṅ manūtra, nara ṅaraniṅ mānuṣa, sakāla ṅaraniṅ samaṅke, yaśa ṅaraniṅ kirti, vidyā ṅaraniṅ aji, aprayadha ṅaraniṅ pūjā,
.</ab>
.
.<ab>
.kaliṅanya, bhaṭāra sira magave pratapa riṅ vana giri, maṅaṣkāra bhaṭāra, bhaṭārī, atitah kasukhan amragat trәṣṇā, anusupi vanavāsa, maṅǝnakǝn tapa, manaṅsāra rāga, tinūt deniṅ manūṣa maṅke, atapa abrata, ayoga asamadhī, ayajña dāna kīrti,
9770</ab>
.
.<ab>
.maṅhanakǝn brata apayapanya, ulandriya, rumәgǝp pañcendriya, tuṅgalakәna riṅ trisandhyā, piṇdhakǝn riṅ kaparāmarthan, vaḍahana yoga, sahabana samadhi, tindihana brata, tuṅgunǝniṅ dāna kīrti, laṅlaṅana riṅ āgama, pagǝrana pupūjān sasapon, lavaṅana saṅgarma, ugǝr ugǝrana sadā, inǝbana tuhu, tindihana kañciṅana parāmartha,
.</ab>
9775
.<ab>
.yeka ulahaniṅ saṅ tumaki-taki kābhyudayan, kābhyudayan ṅaranya, kavibhavan, kavibhavan ṅaranya, bandha savita, bandha savita ṅaranya, kasugihan kula rūpa, śakti vani, niroga nirvighna, cakṣyah lavajjanā, subrata dīrgha yuṣa yovaṇa avet aurip, maṅkana phalaniṅ brata yan inabhyāsa, ya kābhyudayan de saṅ surupa, maṅkana liṅ saṅ citta varaṇa, riṅ saṅ vala kula.
.</ab>
.
9780<ab>
.nambah hulun, mapa riṅ kanirāśrayan, mәne pukulun, mәne kami varah iri kita, lakoni siptaṅku riṅ lagi rumuhun, sājña pukulun, vurukәniṅ brata pukulun, pariñcinya, mvaṅ phalanya, a u ma.]
.</ab>
.</ab>

9785
.

.

.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_312">hana brata, maṅan sәkul sapuluṅ, saṅ hyaṅ maṇik tampa, ṅaraniṅ brata, saṅ hyaṅ maṇḍala hyaṅniṅ brata, ya pinakarūpa, pinakakukusaniṅ śarīra,

10525<div type="translation">
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_00"> om̐. Let there be no obstacle.</p>
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_01">This is the <foreign>Right Behaviour</foreign>
10530 <note>According to the context of this passage, which explains the right behaviour when performing an observance, such as asking permission from the one who in charge in observance, offering betel leaves and reciting mantras, I have chosen <foreign>parikramaning</foreign> ‘proper order of things, right behaviour, customs (ritual) sanctioned by tradition’ (OJED, 1300:8), as attested in mss. N and M. This is instead of <foreign>panarima</foreign>, probably a non-standard form of <foreign>panariman</foreign> ‘he who is given st., recipient’ (OJED, 1953:7.6) as attested in mss. G and P, or <foreign>tiṅkahiṅ panarima</foreign>, meaning ‘way of acting for the recipient’ (the meaning of the word <foreign>tiṅkah</foreign> in OJED is in 2016: 4) as attested in ms. U. The words <foreign>parikrama</foreign>, <foreign>panarima</foreign> and <foreign>tiṅkahiṅ panarima</foreign> in Old Javanese have similar meanings. In the context of observance, the word <foreign>parikramaniṅ brata</foreign> emphasises the process of systematic conduct when performing the observance. Conversely, the word <foreign>panarima brata</foreign> and <foreign>tiṅkahiṅ panarima brata</foreign> emphasises the preparation of the practitioner before performing the observance.</note>
.
. <foreign>in [Performing] Observances</foreign>. When you perform an observance, do not do it haphazardly, without having permission to the one who is in charge of the observances, [namely] the reverend Kaki<note>The word <foreign>kaki</foreign> means ‘grandfather; old man, elder; venerable’ (OJED, 767: 1).</note> Citragopta<note>Citragopta or Citragupta is the keeper of the records of the good and evil deeds of human beings for Yama, and as such is well-known both from Skt. and OJ. literature (his name is also given as Citragotra. In Balinese tradition, he has a famous name as Saṅ Surātma). In <foreign>Kakavin Śivarātrikalpa</foreign> as already mentioned by Teeuw et al. (1969: 52) he reads a book with full account of one’s deed during one’s life. In India the book is called <foreign>Agrasandhāni</foreign>; in the <foreign>Kakavin Śivarātrikalpa</foreign> it is called a <foreign>galih</foreign>, but no specific name is given. </note> [and] Nini<note>The word <foreign>nini</foreign> means ‘grandmother; woman (used in designating or addressing a religious person or an unmarried princess or girl of noble birth)’ (OJED, 1187:4).</note> Citragopta <note>The portrayal of the figure of Nini Citragopta as a female deity alongside Kaki Citragopta prior to the performance of observance in this text is particularly intriguing, as no mention of Nini Citragopta is to be found in the corpus of Old Javanese and Balinese literature. The presence of this figure brings to mind the concept of <foreign>śakti</foreign> in Śaivism. This is one of the key elements indicating the presence of a tantric spirit within this text.</note>
.
. [The request] should be received [by means of] an offering<note>I have chosen to use the word <foreign>caru</foreign> rather than the abbreviation <foreign>ca</foreign> as the abbreviation because it is not commonly found in the corpus of Old Javanese literature. Furthermore, by using the word <foreign>caru</foreign>, which means ‘to have (make, present) as an offering’ (OJED, 310. 6.1), will help readers to understand the meaning of the term directly.</note> of a white and green betel leaf on a well. The mantra is: “My Lord Kaki Citragopta and Nini Citragopta, I ask permission to perform an observance. My Lord, please accompany me when I perform an observance! Everything that I strive after, let it be obtained! If I make a mistake when performing an observance, let it be blamed on the reverend one who is in charge of the observances!” All your observances [will then be] like that.<note>By asking permission to the Kaki Citragopta and Nini Citragopta, practitioners of the observance simultaneously seek protection from them. If they commit a mistake, that mistake is attributed to this deity. This appears to be a tactic employed by practitioners to ensure their safety while performing the observance.
10535</note>
.
.Further, the teeth-polishing leaves [have to be used] by the one who carries out the observances. The exceedingly good one is the <foreign>hambulu</foreign><note><foreign>hambulu, ambulu</foreign> is a part. kind of tree, of the ficus family (Jb.: Ficus infectoria) (OJED, 581:7).</note>; the result is [to become] rich in gold.
.
.There are the teeth-polishing leaves of the <foreign>kayәn</foreign> <note><foreign>kayĕn</foreign> is a part. kind of tree and its flowers. In bal. com. used to render kuyaṅ, q.v. (OJED, 831:12).</note>; the result is many children.
10540
.There are the teeth-polishing leaves of the <foreign>vaṅkal</foreign> <note><foreign>vaṅkal</foreign> is a part. kind of (wild) tree (KBW: a variety of mimosa) (OJED, 2196:6).</note>; the result is [to become] rich in rice.
.
.
.There are the teeth-polishing leaves of the <foreign>lampәni</foreign><note><foreign>lampәni</foreign> is a shrub plant that is about two meters high, the leaves are oval in shape, the young fruit tastes sour, while the old ones taste sweet and are dark red; (KBI, 2016: 717).</note>; the result is that you are successful. The dosage of all the mixtures are the same. It is appropriate to pay full attention to it.
10545
.</p>
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_02">This is the <foreign>Holy Scripture</foreign>
. <note>The word <foreign>tattva</foreign> derived from Sanskrit has many meanings. The OJED defines it as ‘what something is in fact; the facts of the matter; how it really happened; the true story; the essential; the actual; the various categories of reality according to Sāmkhya doctrine; the doctrine concerning reality; the philosophy; the writings containing this doctrine; and really or in reality’ (OJED, 1962: 7). In this context, I have translated the word <foreign>tattva</foreign> as ‘holy scripture’, equating it with <foreign>dharma</foreign> and <foreign>jñāna</foreign> in Old Javanese. Acri (2018: 9) has provided a detailed explanation of the meaning of <foreign>tattva</foreign> and <foreign>jñāna</foreign> as ‘scripture’ in Old Javanese and Sanskrit sources to support this argument.</note> <foreign>on the Observances</foreign>.
10550
.Perfection in observances, its reality is bodiless. The Holy Dharma, its reality is [like] bars of hedge, for it serves as the tie with the reality of the observances [which keeps them together], and [it] also releases supernatural power.<note>This passage discusses the relationship between <foreign>brata</foreign>‘the observance’ and <foreign>dharma</foreign> ‘the truth’. The text explains that the reality of perfection in observances is bodiless. This is why it needs the holy truth as its body to hold everything together. Metaphorically, the truth is referred to as ‘the bars of a hedge’. Here, the metaphor ‘bars of hedge’ indicates that the truth acts as a ‘barrier’ to ensure that, after obtaining supernatural power, the practitioner of the observance still behaves in daily life under the light of Dharma and uses his supernatural power for kindness.</note>
.
.They (i.e., the observances and the Dharma) are just like the left and right bodies.<note> The left body refers to the ‘observances‘ (<foreign>brata</foreign>), and the right body refers to the ‘holy truth‘ (<foreign>dharma</foreign>). The two concepts complement each other</note>.
.
10555The reality of observances and asceticism is likewise.<note>There are two interpretations regarding the use of the word ‘tapa’ here. Firstly, the word ‘tapa’ may be used in parallel with the word ‘dharma’ (‘holy truth’), as explained in the previous sentence. Secondly, the word <foreign>tapa</foreign> is actually used in conjunction with the word <foreign>brata</foreign> (‘observance’). OJED (1945: 5) explains that the word <foreign>tapa</foreign> means ‘religious austerity, bodily mortification, penance, asceticism’. Often in combination with <foreign>brata</foreign>, either ‘the observance of asceticism (penance)’ or ‘penance and other religious observances’.</note>.
.
.That is why, one who strives to obtain goodness should perform [observances and asceticism]. [If] young people perform observances, they will obtain the result of them at a young age. There is nothing that comes into being unless it is performed; there is nothing to be taken from the arrangement [according to] what has been arranged.
.
.
10560As if one cooks rice in the morning and eats it that morning, one cooks rice at noon and eats it that noon, one cooks rice in the evening and eats in that evening. If one is not cooking, one is not eating. [The conclusion is that] the results are according to one’s conduct.
.
.
.Such is the right order of [actions and results]. Because the result of bad and good conduct is obtained, that is why good conduct should be performed without delay. [This] originates from the Holy Scripture on Observances.
.</p>
10565
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_03">This is “The Detailed Enumeration of the Observances”. It should be known.</p>
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_1">There is the observance of ‘cutting off the taste’ (<foreign>mәgat rasa</foreign>): if one eats half [portion], and stands up
10570
.<note>The literal meaning of the word <foreign>sumĕṅka</foreign> is ‘to go upwards, rise, climb’ (OJED, 1740:15.1). In this passage, I have translated it more liberal as ‘stand up’. </note>
.
.for chewing betel. It is fine if one does not speak. After chewing betel, one can eat again. Its appointed duration is one year. The deity is the Goddess Umā. The mantra is: "om̐ mam̐ hail to Umā!" [I take] leave. Its result is that the love of husband and wife is not cut off, and all people love [you].</p>
.
10575
.
.
.
.
10580<p corresp="#tattvabrata_2">There is the observance of ‘eating rice from <foreign>slaṅgi</foreign>’<note>I have choosen the word <foreign>slaṅgi</foreign> as attested in ms. U in the Balinese, which means ‘a pyramid-shaped structure made of aren palm or jackfruit leaves used to display rice during the Kuningan festival’ (KBI, 2016: 987). I have not found the meaning of the word <foreign>ṅgi</foreign> attested in ms. G and N, as well as the word <foreign>ṅgi</foreign> as attested in ms. M, nor of <foreign>gaṅgi</foreign> as attested in ms. P.
.</note>
.(<foreign>amaṅan sәga slaṅgi</foreign>): its duration is seven months. The deity is the Goddess Vastu. The mantra is: "om̐ hail to the Goddess Vastu!" [I take ] leave. Its result is that the love of husband and wife is not cut off, and all people<note>I have emended the phrase <foreign>sama janma</foreign> attested in G M N U and <foreign>janma kabeh</foreign> attested in P to <foreign>samanta janma</foreign> ‘all people’. I made this decision in the light of previous passage 3.1 <foreign>mvaṅ samanta janma paḍa sih</foreign> ‘and all people love [you]’.</note> love you and feel sympathy for you.
.</p>
.
10585 <p corresp="#tattvabrata_3"> There is the observance of the ‘earth-leaf’ (<foreign>bhūmipāttra</foreign>): if one eats without using leaves, and lays [the food] openly on earth. The deity is reverend Vaiśravaṇa. Its appointed duration is one year and seven months. The mantra is: “om̐ <note> have chosen the word <foreign>śrī</foreign>, which is attested in P, instead of <foreign>śram̐</foreign> in G, <foreign>sam̐</foreign> in M and N, and <foreign>śi</foreign> in U. This is because in other passages of this text, such as 3.7 <foreign>om̐ śrī ratih devyai namaḥ</foreign>, 3.10 <foreign>om̐ śrī smarāya namaḥ</foreign>, 3.11 <foreign>om̐ śrī śrī devyai namaḥ</foreign>, etc., the word <foreign>śrī</foreign> is used instead of the other <foreign>bījamantra</foreign>. The <foreign>bījamantra</foreign>s like <foreign>śram̐</foreign> in G, <foreign>sam̐</foreign> in M and N, and <foreign>śi</foreign> are not appropriate in this context. In the Indian tradition, the reverend Vaiśravaṇa is often identified with Kubera. He is the guardian of the northern direction and his home is in the northern quadrant of the topmost tier of the lower half of Mount Meru.
.</note> hail to the illustrious Vaiśravaṇa!” [I take ] leave. Its result is being rich in land and freeholds, and you are loved by the king and priests.
.
.</p>
.
10590
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_4">There is the observance of ‘craving to embroider’ (<foreign>anulam iḍam</foreign>)<note>I have conjectured <foreign>nulam idhan</foreign> in G, <foreign>nulam iḍam</foreign> in M, N and U, and <foreign>nulambhi nan</foreign> in P to <foreign>anulam iḍam</foreign> ‘craving to embroider’. This word has been conjectured to convey the proper meaning in Old Javanese. The word <foreign>anulam</foreign> is derived from the word <foreign>sulam</foreign>, meaning ‘to embroider’ (OJED s.v.), and the word <foreign>iḍam</foreign> means ‘to experience the cravings of pregnancy, to be pregnant’ (OJED, 665 7: 1). Thus, the word <foreign>anulam iḍam</foreign> can be translated as ‘craving to embroider’. </note>: one fast all day, until the end of the day. Its appointed duration is three months. Its result is that all desires will be obtained quickly because of that. You will be beloved by men. The deity is the Reverend Brahmā. Mantra: “om̐ Am̐ hail to Brahmā!” [I take] leave.</p>
.
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_5">There is the observance of eating before the Reverend Sun goes down. Its appointed duration is three years. The deity of the observance is the Lord Śiva. Its result is that the mind will be clear. Your thoughts are alive <note> In this context, the phrase ‘thought will be alive’ refers to a state of mind full of inspiration. It is also suitable with the technique of the observance that has a link to the Reverend Sun as the origin of all light in this world, and is also in accordance with the belief that the Reverend Sun is the origin of all light in this world.
10595</note> in one goal. Mantra: “om̐ Mam̐ hail to Śiva!” If you apply make up.
.</p>
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_6">There is the observance of not eating when the Reverend Sun is already at sunset. Its appointed duration is one year. The deity is the Reverend Śiva. The mantra is: “om̐, hail to Śiva!” [I take] leave. Its result is that one will be knowledgeable in every kind of work, especially in learning; and one will not be ignorant in playing the <foreign>gamәlan</foreign> <note> <foreign>gamәlan</foreign> is percussion instrument, ensemble of percussion instruments (OJED, 483:1.3). </note>, telling a story, and [composing] <foreign>kakavin</foreign> <note><foreign>kakavin</foreign> is poem (in Indian metres) (OJED, 826:3.7).</note>; one will be handsome without equal.
.</p>
10600
. <p corresp="#tattvabrata_7">There is the observance of ‘full moon’ (<foreign>mūrṇama</foreign>): you are fasting every full moon. Its appointed duration is seven years and seven months. The deity is the Goddess Ratih. Mantra: “om̐ hail to Śrī Ratih!” [I take] leave. Its result is that your work will be successful, God and Demon will love you.
.</p>
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_8">There is the observance of ‘dark moon’ (<foreign>nilәm</foreign>): you are fasting every dark moon. Its appointed duration is seven months. The deity is the Goddess Rātri Devi. The mantra is: “om̐ hail to Rātri Devi!” [I take leave]. Its result is that you will be loved by mankind; God and Demon will love you.</p>
10605
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_9">There is the observance of ‘the abundance’ <note> In the light of Sanskrit (Monier-Williams, 1182), I translate the name of this observance, <foreign>Narasvatī</foreign>, as ‘the abundance’ instead of ‘acting like Sarasvatī’, due to the absence of a link between Sarasvatī, the goddess of knowledge, and the deity and mantra in this observance. According to the deity of this passage, Rāja Lakṣmi, who is revered as the goddess of happiness, fortune, wealth, prosperity, beauty, fertility, sovereignty and abundance, this translation is appropriate. </note> (<foreign>Narasvatī</foreign>): one does not eat the cooked rice [that is cooked with] abundant water. It is only the rice cone without meat, just salt. Its appointed duration is one year and seven months. The deity is Goddess Rāja Lakṣmi. The mantra is: “om̐ hail to Śri Rāja Lakṣmi!” [I take] leave. Its result is that your good qualities will come out, and all your aims will be fulfilled, and then you will be famous, and you will be in harmony with your spouse.
.</p>
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_10">There is the observance of ‘always in bloom’ <note>Other posibility to translate this term are ‘always worshiping with flowers’, ‘always arranging flowers’, and
10610‘always wearing flowers’. </note> (<foreign>muṣpasadā</foreign>): when one should eat the flower as meat first. Its appointed duration is one year. The deity is Reverend Smara. The mantra is: “om̐ hail to Smara!” [I take] leave. Its result is that one’s face is matchless; many [people] will love you deeply.
.</p>
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_11">There is the observance of ‘applying salve’ (<foreign>ṅlepana</foreign>): when one eats the side dish<note>In Modern Javanese, the word <foreign>lalab</foreign> refers to ‘uncooked fruit and leaves eaten with rice’ (OJED, 962:2), whereas in Balinese, it refers to ‘boiled food’ (KBI, 2016: 290).</note> as meat first. Its appointed duration is three years. The deity is the Goddess Śrī. The mantra is: “om̐ hail to Śrī!”. [I take] leave. Its result is your face being beautiful and calm, being rich in rice, many people will love you and have sympathy for you.</p>
.
10615<p corresp="#tattvabrata_12">There is the observance of not chewing betel. Its appointed duration is one year, and one month. The deity is the Reverend Manodeva<note> I have chosen the word <foreign>manodeva</foreign> attested in ms. M and N, rather than <foreign>aśvino</foreign> attested in ms. G; <foreign>asvido</foreign> attested in ms. P; and <foreign>maṣnodeva</foreign> attested in ms. U because the word <foreign>manodeva</foreign> is quite similar to <foreign>Manobhava</foreign> as the god of love (see OJED, 1105: 03). This phenomenon is probably similar to the localisation of the god Manobhu in the context of Bali. The word manodeva is also appropriate to the dative mantra <foreign>manodevāya</foreign> when compared to the others in this passage. Another important reason is that the result of this observance is <foreign>meṅət rūpanta manis, mvaṅ akveh bhrānta hyun iri kita</foreign>: ‘your face will be sweet and deeply loved, and many people will fall in love with you.’ This result of the observance is strongly related to the Manobhava as mentioned in 3.10 <foreign>riṅ rūpa tan pasiriṅ, akveh rәsəp asih iri kita</foreign>, and 3.203 <foreign>pinakarūpa, aśrī sumilah</foreign>.</note>. The mantra is: “om̐ hail to Manodeva!” [I take] leave. Its result is that your face will be sweet [and] deeply loved, and many people will be sick with love for you</p>
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_13">There is the observance of ‘easy breath’<note> Another alternative translation of <foreign>lәga prāṇa</foreign> is ‘contented life’. Literally, the word <foreign>lәga</foreign> means ‘open, satisfied, content, relieved; taking lightly, accepting, renouncing readily’ (OJED, 1001:10), and the word <foreign>prāṇa</foreign> means ‘1. breath; first of the five vital airs (see pañcabāyu); 2. the breath of life, life; 3. (as a seat of the feelings:) heart, soul; 4. the place on the body where one can be mortally wounded (where one’s life is located), esp. the breast; mortal (of a wound); 5. numeral coefficient for living creatures’ (OJED, 1394:9). </note> (<foreign>lәga prāṇa</foreign>): if one eats carrying a kris on his lap. Its appointed duration is one year and seven months. The mantra is: “Om hail to Rudra!” [I take] leave. Its result is that many people will be ready to sacrifice their lives for your life; many people will be compassionate and will love you.
.
.</p>
10620<p corresp="#tattvabrata_14">There is the observance of ‘hero’<note>I assume that the word <foreign>bīra</foreign> here is the other form of <foreign>vīra</foreign> which is refers to brave man, hero, valiant warrior; brave, valiant (OJED, 2289: 6). This phenomenon is often in Old Javanese, for instance the word <foreign>bulan</foreign> ‘moon’ also has other form as <foreign>vulan</foreign>.</note> (<foreign>bīra</foreign>): if one eats salt as meat. Its appointed duration is one year and three months. The deity is the Lord Iśvara. The mantra is: “om̐ mam̐ hail to Īśvara!” [I take leave]. Its result is that all your efforts will be achieved quickly; you will be loved by mankind, and the Gods [and] the Demons will love you.
.</p>
.
.

However, on the waning moon, it should decrease by a handful every day. Finally, one fasts when the dark moon. Its appointed duration is three months.

.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_279">There is the observance of ‘thursday’: the manner is one fasts every thursday. Its result is that you will be beautiful, and all your works will be good.</p>

mrakih NThis […] Behaviour According to the context of this passage, which explains the right behaviour when performing an observance, such as asking permission from the one who in charge in observance, offering betel leaves and reciting mantras, I have chosen parikramaning ‘proper order of things, right behaviour, customs (ritual) sanctioned by tradition’ (OJED, 1300:8), as attested in mss. N and M. This is instead of panarima, probably a non-standard form of panariman ‘he who is given st., recipient’ (OJED, 1953:7.6) as attested in mss. G and P, or tiṅkahiṅ panarima, meaning ‘way of acting for the recipient’ (the meaning of the word tiṅkah in OJED is in 2016: 4) as attested in ms. U. The words parikrama, panarima and tiṅkahiṅ panarima in Old Javanese have similar meanings. In the context of observance, the word parikramaniṅ brata emphasises the process of systematic conduct when performing the observance. Conversely, the word panarima brata and tiṅkahiṅ panarima brata emphasises the preparation of the practitioner before performing the observance. in [Performing] Observances. When you perform an observance, do not do it haphazardly, without having permission to the one who is in charge of the observances, [namely] the reverend KakiThe word kaki means ‘grandfather; old man, elder; venerable’ (OJED, 767: 1). CitragoptaCitragopta or Citragupta is the keeper of the records of the good and evil deeds of human beings for Yama, and as such is well-known both from Skt. and OJ. literature (his name is also given as Citragotra. In Balinese tradition, he has a famous name as Saṅ Surātma). In Kakavin Śivarātrikalpa as already mentioned by Teeuw et al. (1969: 52) he reads a book with full account of one’s deed during one’s life. In India the book is called Agrasandhāni; in the Kakavin Śivarātrikalpa it is called a galih, but no specific name is given. [and] NiniThe word nini means ‘grandmother; woman (used in designating or addressing a religious person or an unmarried princess or girl of noble birth)’ (OJED, 1187:4). Citragopta The portrayal of the figure of Nini Citragopta as a female deity alongside Kaki Citragopta prior to the performance of observance in this text is particularly intriguing, as no mention of Nini Citragopta is to be found in the corpus of Old Javanese and Balinese literature. The presence of this figure brings to mind the concept of śakti in Śaivism. This is one of the key elements indicating the presence of a tantric spirit within this text. [The request] should be received [by means of] an offeringI have chosen to use the word caru rather than the abbreviation ca as the abbreviation because it is not commonly found in the corpus of Old Javanese literature. Furthermore, by using the word caru, which means ‘to have (make, present) as an offering’ (OJED, 310. 6.1), will help readers to understand the meaning of the term directly. of a white and green betel leaf on a well. The mantra is: “My Lord Kaki Citragopta and Nini Citragopta, I ask permission to perform an observance. My Lord, please accompany me when I perform an observance! Everything that I strive after, let it be obtained! If I make a mistake when performing an observance, let it be blamed on the reverend one who is in charge of the observances!” All your observances [will then be] like that.By asking permission to the Kaki Citragopta and Nini Citragopta, practitioners of the observance simultaneously seek protection from them. If they commit a mistake, that mistake is attributed to this deity. This appears to be a tactic employed by practitioners to ensure their safety while performing the observance. Further, the teeth-polishing leaves [have to be used] by the one who carries out the observances. The exceedingly good one is the hambuluhambulu, ambulu is a part. kind of tree, of the ficus family (Jb.: Ficus infectoria) (OJED, 581:7).; the result is [to become] rich in gold. There are the teeth-polishing leaves of the kayәn kayĕn is a part. kind of tree and its flowers. In bal. com. used to render kuyaṅ, q.v. (OJED, 831:12).; the result is many children. There are the teeth-polishing leaves of the vaṅkal vaṅkal is a part. kind of (wild) tree (KBW: a variety of mimosa) (OJED, 2196:6).; the result is [to become] rich in rice. There are the teeth-polishing leaves of the lampәnilampәni is a shrub plant that is about two meters high, the leaves are oval in shape, the young fruit tastes sour, while the old ones taste sweet and are dark red; (KBI, 2016: 717).; the result is that you are successful. The dosage of all the mixtures are the same. It is appropriate to pay full attention to it.

(1969: 52) he reads a book with full account of one’s deed during one’s life. In India the book is called Agrasandhāni; in the Kakavin Śivarātrikalpa it is called a galih, but no specific name is given. [and] NiniThe word nini means ‘grandmother; woman (used in designating or addressing a religious person or an unmarried princess or girl of noble birth)’ (OJED, 1187:4). Citragopta The portrayal of the figure of Nini Citragopta as a female deity alongside Kaki Citragopta prior to the performance of observance in this text is particularly intriguing, as no mention of Nini Citragopta is to be found in the corpus of Old Javanese and Balinese literature. The presence of this figure brings to mind the concept of śakti in Śaivism. This is one of the key elements indicating the presence of a tantric spirit within this text. [The request] should be received [by means of] an offeringI have chosen to use the word caru rather than the abbreviation ca as the abbreviation because it is not commonly found in the corpus of Old Javanese literature. Furthermore, by using the word caru, which means ‘to have (make, present) as an offering’ (OJED, 310. 6.1), will help readers to understand the meaning of the term directly. of a white and green betel leaf on a well. The mantra is: “My Lord Kaki Citragopta and Nini Citragopta, I ask permission to perform an observance. My Lord, please accompany me when I perform an observance! Everything that I strive after, let it be obtained! If I make a mistake when performing an observance, let it be blamed on the reverend one who is in charge of the observances!” All your observances [will then be] like that.By asking permission to the Kaki Citragopta and Nini Citragopta, practitioners of the observance simultaneously seek protection from them. If they commit a mistake, that mistake is attributed to this deity. This appears to be a tactic employed by practitioners to ensure their safety while performing the observance. Further, the teeth-polishing leaves [have to be used] by the one who carries out the observances. The exceedingly good one is the hambuluhambulu, ambulu is a part. kind of tree, of the ficus family (Jb.: Ficus infectoria) (OJED, 581:7).; the result is [to become] rich in gold. There are the teeth-polishing leaves of the kayәn kayĕn is a part. kind of tree and its flowers. In bal. com. used to render kuyaṅ, q.v. (OJED, 831:12).; the result is many children. There are the teeth-polishing leaves of the vaṅkal vaṅkal is a part. kind of (wild) tree (KBW: a variety of mimosa) (OJED, 2196:6).; the result is [to become] rich in rice. There are the teeth-polishing leaves of the lampәnilampәni is a shrub plant that is about two meters high, the leaves are oval in shape, the young fruit tastes sour, while the old ones taste sweet and are dark red; (KBI, 2016: 717).; the result is that you are successful. The dosage of all the mixtures are the same. It is appropriate to pay full attention to it.
Citragopta or Citragupta is the keeper of the records of the good and evil deeds of human beings for Yama, and as such is well-known both from Skt. and OJ. literature (his name is also given as Citragotra. In Balinese tradition, he has a famous name as Saṅ Surātma). In Kakavin Śivarātrikalpa as already mentioned by Teeuw et al. (1969: 52) he reads a book with full account of one’s deed during one’s life. In India the book is called Agrasandhāni; in the Kakavin Śivarātrikalpa it is called a galih, but no specific name is given. This […] Behaviour According to the context of this passage, which explains the right behaviour when performing an observance, such as asking permission from the one who in charge in observance, offering betel leaves and reciting mantras, I have chosen parikramaning ‘proper order of things, right behaviour, customs (ritual) sanctioned by tradition’ (OJED, 1300:8), as attested in mss. N and M. This is instead of panarima, probably a non-standard form of panariman ‘he who is given st., recipient’ (OJED, 1953:7.6) as attested in mss. G and P, or tiṅkahiṅ panarima, meaning ‘way of acting for the recipient’ (the meaning of the word tiṅkah in OJED is in 2016: 4) as attested in ms. U. The words parikrama, panarima and tiṅkahiṅ panarima in Old Javanese have similar meanings. In the context of observance, the word parikramaniṅ brata emphasises the process of systematic conduct when performing the observance. Conversely, the word panarima brata and tiṅkahiṅ panarima brata emphasises the preparation of the practitioner before performing the observance. in [Performing] Observances. When you perform an observance, do not do it haphazardly, without having permission to the one who is in charge of the observances, [namely] the reverend KakiThe word kaki means ‘grandfather; old man, elder; venerable’ (OJED, 767: 1). Conversely, the word panarima brata and tiṅkahiṅ panarima brata emphasises the preparation of the practitioner before performing the observance. in [Performing] Observances. When you perform an observance, do not do it haphazardly, without having permission to the one who is in charge of the observances, [namely] the reverend KakiThe word kaki means ‘grandfather; old man, elder; venerable’ (OJED, 767: 1). CitragoptaCitragopta or Citragupta is the keeper of the records of the good and evil deeds of human beings for Yama, and as such is well-known both from Skt. and OJ. literature (his name is also given as Citragotra. In Balinese tradition, he has a famous name as Saṅ Surātma). In Kakavin Śivarātrikalpa as already mentioned by Teeuw et al. (1969: 52) he reads a book with full account of one’s deed during one’s life. In India the book is called Agrasandhāni; in the Kakavin Śivarātrikalpa it is called a galih, but no specific name is given. [and] NiniThe word nini means ‘grandmother; woman (used in designating or addressing a religious person or an unmarried princess or girl of noble birth)’ (OJED, 1187:4). Citragopta The portrayal of the figure of Nini Citragopta as a female deity alongside Kaki Citragopta prior to the performance of observance in this text is particularly intriguing, as no mention of Nini Citragopta is to be found in the corpus of Old Javanese and Balinese literature. The presence of this figure brings to mind the concept of śakti in Śaivism. This is one of the key elements indicating the presence of a tantric spirit within this text. [The request] should be received [by means of] an offeringI have chosen to use the word caru rather than the abbreviation ca as the abbreviation because it is not commonly found in the corpus of Old Javanese literature. Furthermore, by using the word caru, which means ‘to have (make, present) as an offering’ (OJED, 310. 6.1), will help readers to understand the meaning of the term directly. of a white and green betel leaf on a well. The mantra is: “My Lord Kaki Citragopta and Nini Citragopta, I ask permission to perform an observance. My Lord, please accompany me when I perform an observance! Everything that I strive after, let it be obtained! If I make a mistake when performing an observance, let it be blamed on the reverend one who is in charge of the observances!” All your observances [will then be] like that.By asking permission to the Kaki Citragopta and Nini Citragopta, practitioners of the observance simultaneously seek protection from them. If they commit a mistake, that mistake is attributed to this deity. This appears to be a tactic employed by practitioners to ensure their safety while performing the observance. Further, the teeth-polishing leaves [have to be used] by the one who carries out the observances. The exceedingly good one is the hambuluhambulu, ambulu is a part. kind of tree, of the ficus family (Jb.: Ficus infectoria) (OJED, 581:7).; the result is [to become] rich in gold. There are the teeth-polishing leaves of the kayәn kayĕn is a part. kind of tree and its flowers. In bal. com. used to render kuyaṅ, q.v. (OJED, 831:12).; the result is many children. There are the teeth-polishing leaves of the vaṅkal vaṅkal is a part. kind of (wild) tree (KBW: a variety of mimosa) (OJED, 2196:6).; the result is [to become] rich in rice. There are the teeth-polishing leaves of the lampәnilampәni is a shrub plant that is about two meters high, the leaves are oval in shape, the young fruit tastes sour, while the old ones taste sweet and are dark red; (KBI, 2016: 717).; the result is that you are successful. The dosage of all the mixtures are the same. It is appropriate to pay full attention to it.

lampәni is a shrub plant that is about two meters high, the leaves are oval in shape, the young fruit tastes sour, while the old ones taste sweet and are dark red; (KBI, 2016: 717).This […] Scripture The word tattva derived from Sanskrit has many meanings. The OJED defines it as ‘what something is in fact; the facts of the matter; how it really happened; the true story; the essential; the actual; the various categories of reality according to Sāmkhya doctrine; the doctrine concerning reality; the philosophy; the writings containing this doctrine; and really or in reality’ (OJED, 1962: 7). In this context, I have translated the word tattva as ‘holy scripture’, equating it with dharma and jñāna in Old Javanese. Acri (2018: 9) has provided a detailed explanation of the meaning of tattva and jñāna as ‘scripture’ in Old Javanese and Sanskrit sources to support this argument. on the Observances. Perfection in observances, its reality is bodiless. The Holy Dharma, its reality is [like] bars of hedge, for it serves as the tie with the reality of the observances [which keeps them together], and [it] also releases supernatural power.This passage discusses the relationship between brata‘the observance’ and dharma ‘the truth’. The text explains that the reality of perfection in observances is bodiless. This is why it needs the holy truth as its body to hold everything together. Metaphorically, the truth is referred to as ‘the bars of a hedge’. Here, the metaphor ‘bars of hedge’ indicates that the truth acts as a ‘barrier’ to ensure that, after obtaining supernatural power, the practitioner of the observance still behaves in daily life under the light of Dharma and uses his supernatural power for kindness. They (i.e., the observances and the Dharma) are just like the left and right bodies. The left body refers to the ‘observances‘ (brata), and the right body refers to the ‘holy truth‘ (dharma). The two concepts complement each other. The reality of observances and asceticism is likewise.There are two interpretations regarding the use of the word ‘tapa’ here. Firstly, the word ‘tapa’ may be used in parallel with the word ‘dharma’ (‘holy truth’), as explained in the previous sentence. Secondly, the word tapa is actually used in conjunction with the word brata (‘observance’). OJED (1945: 5) explains that the word tapa means ‘religious austerity, bodily mortification, penance, asceticism’. Often in combination with brata, either ‘the observance of asceticism (penance)’ or ‘penance and other religious observances’.. That is why, one who strives to obtain goodness should perform [observances and asceticism]. [If] young people perform observances, they will obtain the result of them at a young age. There is nothing that comes into being unless it is performed; there is nothing to be taken from the arrangement [according to] what has been arranged. As if one cooks rice in the morning and eats it that morning, one cooks rice at noon and eats it that noon, one cooks rice in the evening and eats in that evening. If one is not cooking, one is not eating. [The conclusion is that] the results are according to one’s conduct. Such is the right order of [actions and results]. Because the result of bad and good conduct is obtained, that is why good conduct should be performed without delay. [This] originates from the Holy Scripture on Observances.

I have emended the phrase sama janma attested in G M N U and janma kabeh attested in P to samanta janma ‘all people’. I made this decision in the light of previous passage 3.1 mvaṅ samanta janma paḍa sih ‘and all people love [you]’. […] Meru. hail to the illustrious Vaiśravaṇa!” [I take ] leave. Its result is being rich in land and freeholds, and you are loved by the king and priests.
have chosen the word śrī, which is attested in P, instead of śram̐ in G, sam̐ in M and N, and śi in U. This is because in other passages of this text, such as 3.7 om̐ śrī ratih devyai namaḥ, 3.10 om̐ śrī smarāya namaḥ, 3.11 om̐ śrī śrī devyai namaḥ, etc., the word śrī is used instead of the other bījamantra. The bījamantras like śram̐ in G, sam̐ in M and N, and śi are not appropriate in this context. In the Indian tradition, the reverend Vaiśravaṇa is often identified with Kubera. He is the guardian of the northern direction and his home is in the northern quadrant of the topmost tier of the lower half of Mount Meru. There […] leave.
I have conjectured nulam idhan in G, nulam iḍam in M, N and U, and nulambhi nan in P to anulam iḍam ‘craving to embroider’. This word has been conjectured to convey the proper meaning in Old Javanese. The word anulam is derived from the word sulam, meaning ‘to embroider’ (OJED s.v.), and the word iḍam means ‘to experience the cravings of pregnancy, to be pregnant’ (OJED, 665 7: 1). Thus, the word anulam iḍam can be translated as ‘craving to embroider’. There […] world. in one goal. Mantra: “om̐ Mam̐ hail to Śiva!” If you apply make up.
In this context, the phrase ‘thought will be alive’ refers to a state of mind full of inspiration. It is also suitable with the technique of the observance that has a link to the Reverend Sun as the origin of all light in this world, and is also in accordance with the belief that the Reverend Sun is the origin of all light in this world. kakavin is poem (in Indian metres) (OJED, 826:3.7).There […] spouse.
In the light of Sanskrit (Monier-Williams, 1182), I translate the name of this observance, Narasvatī, as ‘the abundance’ instead of ‘acting like Sarasvatī’, due to the absence of a link between Sarasvatī, the goddess of knowledge, and the deity and mantra in this observance. According to the deity of this passage, Rāja Lakṣmi, who is revered as the goddess of happiness, fortune, wealth, prosperity, beauty, fertility, sovereignty and abundance, this translation is appropriate. There […] ‘always wearing flowers’. (muṣpasadā): when one should eat the flower as meat first. Its appointed duration is one year. The deity is Reverend Smara. The mantra is: “om̐ hail to Smara!” [I take] leave. Its result is that one’s face is matchless; many [people] will love you deeply.
Other posibility to translate this term are ‘always worshiping with flowers’, ‘always arranging flowers’, and ‘always wearing flowers’. There […] you.
In Modern Javanese, the word lalab refers to ‘uncooked fruit and leaves eaten with rice’ (OJED, 962:2), whereas in Balinese, it refers to ‘boiled food’ (KBI, 2016: 290).There […] you
I have chosen the word manodeva attested in ms. M and N, rather than aśvino attested in ms. G; asvido attested in ms. P; and maṣnodeva attested in ms. U because the word manodeva is quite similar to Manobhava as the god of love (see OJED, 1105: 03). This phenomenon is probably similar to the localisation of the god Manobhu in the context of Bali. The word manodeva is also appropriate to the dative mantra manodevāya when compared to the others in this passage. Another important reason is that the result of this observance is meṅət rūpanta manis, mvaṅ akveh bhrānta hyun iri kita: ‘your face will be sweet and deeply loved, and many people will fall in love with you.’ This result of the observance is strongly related to the Manobhava as mentioned in 3.10 riṅ rūpa tan pasiriṅ, akveh rәsəp asih iri kita, and 3.203 pinakarūpa, aśrī sumilah.There […] you.
Another alternative translation of lәga prāṇa is ‘contented life’. Literally, the word lәga means ‘open, satisfied, content, relieved; taking lightly, accepting, renouncing readily’ (OJED, 1001:10), and the word prāṇa means ‘1. breath; first of the five vital airs (see pañcabāyu); 2. the breath of life, life; 3. (as a seat of the feelings:) heart, soul; 4. the place on the body where one can be mortally wounded (where one’s life is located), esp. the breast; mortal (of a wound); 5. numeral coefficient for living creatures’ (OJED, 1394:9). I assume that the word bīra here is the other form of vīra which is refers to brave man, hero, valiant warrior; brave, valiant (OJED, 2289: 6). This phenomenon is often in Old Javanese, for instance the word bulan ‘moon’ also has other form as vulan.
